ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, point D is on line AB. When $\triangle ABC$ is folded along CD, point A falls on side BC at point A. If $\angle B=35^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BDA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Since $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $\angle B=35^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle A=180^\circ-\angle ACB-\angle B=180^\circ-90^\circ-35^\circ=55^\circ$, \\
Since $\triangle CDA$ is obtained by folding $\triangle CDA$, \\
thus $\angle CAD=\angle A=55^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle CAD=\angle B+\angle BDA=\angle B+20^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle BDA=\angle CAD-\angle B=55^\circ-35^\circ=\boxed{20^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the figure: in the figure, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is above, and D is on AB; after folding along CD, A falls to A' on BC, and DA' is drawn. Therefore the problem actually asks for the angle at D between DB and DA'. Then reason: because ∠ACB=90°, and ∠B=35°, ∠A=180°−90°−35°=55°. Also because D is on AB, ∠CAD is the angle of △ABC at A, equal to 55°. After folding about CD, A maps to A', so the corresponding angle ∠CA'D=55°. Since C, A', B are collinear, ∠CA'D is the exterior angle of △BA'D at A', therefore ∠CA'D=∠DBA'+∠BDA'. And DB lies along AB, BA' lies along BC, so ∠DBA'=∠B=35°. Hence ∠BDA'=55°−35°=20°.
